items.stem: Which type of mirror forms an image that is always erect and smaller than the object?
Based on the passage, which of the following is true about the image formed by a convex mirror?
If a person stands in front of a mirror and the image of the person is smaller and erect, which type of mirror is most likely being used?
If an object is placed very close to a concave mirror, what type of image is formed?
Which mirror is used in the side-view mirrors of vehicles to provide a wider field of view?
A student observes that an object placed at a certain distance from a mirror produces a virtual and enlarged image. Which type of mirror could this be?
In the experiment shown in Fig. 10.8, when the angle of incidence increases, what happens to the angle of reflection?
A person standing in front of a mirror notices that the image of a distant object is seen only when the mirror is placed at a certain distance. What could be the reason for this?

A student is given a mirror and told that it is either concave or convex. When an object is placed very close to the mirror, the image is erect and larger than the object. What can be concluded about the mirror?
What happens when multiple parallel beams of light fall on a concave mirror?
What is the purpose of the oil or wax used in the activity with the water drop?
A student holds a concave mirror facing the Sun and directs the reflected light onto a paper. After a while, the paper starts to burn. What is the reason for this?
If an object is placed at the focal point of a concave mirror, what kind of image is formed?
What kind of lens is thinner at the middle compared to its edges?
Which type of lens diverges light beams?
What happens to a light beam when it passes through a convex lens?
A student observes that an object appears erect and diminished when viewed through a lens. Which type of lens is the student using?
Which type of mirror forms an image that is always erect and diminished in size?

A man walks in front of a mirror and parallel to it at a distance twice the distance of the light source from the mirror. What is the greatest distance over which he can see the image of the light source in the mirror?
A woman walks towards a large concave mirror. What will she see?
In Fig. 10.27, O stands for object, M for mirror, and I for image. Which statement is true?
Which of the following is true when light is incident along the normal on a mirror?
Which of the following is a property of a plane mirror?

A point source of light B is placed at a distance d in front of the centre of a mirror of horizontal length L. A man walks in front of the mirror and parallel to it at a distance 2d from it. What is the greatest distance over which he can see the image of the light source in the mirror?
Why are convex mirrors preferred for observing the traffic behind us?
What is the name of a lens that is thicker at the edges than in the middle?
Which type of lens always forms an erect and diminished image of an object?
If a convex lens is used to focus sunlight onto a piece of paper, what kind of image is formed?
What happens to a parallel beam of light when it passes through a concave lens?
A student places an object behind a convex lens and observes that the image is inverted and enlarged. What can be inferred about the object's position relative to the lens?
What happens to multiple parallel light beams when they fall on a concave mirror?
What is the purpose of using a concave mirror in the experiment described in the passage?
Which type of mirror is used as a reflector in torches and headlights?
A student observes that after reflecting from a mirror, the light rays converge at a point. Which type of mirror is most likely being used?
In the experiment with the water drop, the text under the drop appears larger. What explains this phenomenon?
A student sets up a mirror and shines a light beam on it. When the sheet of paper is bent, the reflected beam disappears. What does this demonstrate?

A student observes an object placed in front of a spherical mirror. The image formed is erect, smaller than the object, and does not change size as the object is moved closer or farther. Which type of mirror is most likely being used?
According to the law of reflection, what is the relationship between the angle of incidence and the angle of reflection?
Which of the following statements about the use of mirrors is correct?
What is the function of the normal line in the law of reflection?
In a reflecting telescope, what is the primary function of the main mirror?
What is the function of a convex lens?
A convex lens is used to focus the light from a distant object. What happens to the light rays?
